evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is characterized by significantly elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) that leads to atherosclerotic plaque deposition in the coronary arteries and proximal aorta at an early age and increases the risk of premature cardiovascular events such as angina and myocardial infarction; stroke occurs more rarely.

nodes.description: Smooth muscle cells produce collagen, proteoglycans and elastin within the developing plaque. A fibrous cap can stabilize the lesion; matrix accumulation is not equated with cap degradation.

nodes.description: Enlarging plaques can narrow arteries and impair perfusion. Compensatory remodeling and nonobstructive plaques mean that plaque burden is not identical to stenosis. This chronic flow-limiting branch is separate from acute rupture and thrombosis.

evidence.snippet: Coronary artery-related manifestations and peripheral artery disease were more prevalent in FH patients than in controls, but no significant differences were found for cerebrovascular events.

evidence.reference_title: Familial hypercholesterolemia and atherosclerosis in cloned minipigs created by DNA transposition of a human PCSK9 gain-of-function mutant.

nodes.description: Elevated plasma LDL cholesterol concentration is the measured abnormality used both for diagnosis and for monitoring treatment response.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: A clinical diagnosis of FH can be established in a proband with characteristic clinical features and significantly elevated LDL-C levels (typically >190 mg/dL in adults and >160 mg/dL in children).

nodes.description: Fully human monoclonal antibody that binds circulating PCSK9 and prevents it from engaging the hepatocyte LDL receptor, restoring receptor recycling and hepatic LDL clearance. In heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia it lowers LDL cholesterol by approximately 60% on top of statin therapy, and in established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease it reduces cardiovascular events. It is the mechanistically direct therapy for ADH3: the drug target is PCSK9 itself.

evidence.reference_title: PCSK9 inhibition with evolocumab (AMG 145) in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (RUTHERFORD-2): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: In patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, evolocumab administered either 140 mg every 2 weeks or 420 mg monthly was well tolerated and yielded similar and rapid 60% reductions in LDL cholesterol compared with placebo.

evidence.reference_title: Evolocumab and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.
evidence.snippet: In our trial, inhibition of PCSK9 with evolocumab on a background of statin therapy lowered LDL cholesterol levels to a median of 30 mg per deciliter (0.78 mmol per liter) and reduced the risk of cardiovascular events.

nodes.description: Sustained cholesterol excess can produce deposits in tendons, periocular skin and the corneal margin. The sites are distinct clinical expressions of cholesterol deposition and are variably present.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Xanthomas (cholesterol deposits in tendons) may be visible in the Achilles tendons or tendons of the hands and worsen with age as a result of extremely high cholesterol levels.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Xanthelasmas (yellowish, waxy deposits) can occur around the eyelids.

evidence.reference_title: Severe hypercholesterolemia in four British families with the D374Y mutation in the PCSK9 gene: long-term follow-up and treatment response.
evidence.snippet: These British PCSK9 patients with the D374Y mutation have an unpredictably severe clinical phenotype, which may be a unique feature for this cohort, and requires early and aggressive lipid-lowering management to prevent cardiovascular complications.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations and polymorphisms in the proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin 9 (PCSK9) gene in cholesterol metabolism and disease.
evidence.snippet: Several PCSK9 variants have been identified, some of them are gain-of-function mutations causing hypercholesterolemia by a reduction of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor levels; while others are loss-of-function variants associated with a reduction of LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and a decreased risk of CHD.

nodes.description: A small interfering RNA that silences PCSK9 messenger RNA in the hepatocyte, suppressing synthesis of the protein rather than neutralising it after secretion. Given twice yearly after loading. In heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia it lowered LDL cholesterol by roughly 40% versus baseline (about 48 percentage points versus placebo), with reductions reported across FH genotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Inclisiran for the Treatment of Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Among adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, those who received inclisiran had significantly lower levels of LDL cholesterol than those who received placebo, with an infrequent dosing regimen and an acceptable safety profile.

evidence.reference_title: Inclisiran for the Treatment of Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: There were robust reductions in LDL cholesterol levels in all genotypes of familial hypercholesterolemia.

nodes.description: Whole-gene duplication can increase circulating PCSK9 abundance. A concentration near 5000 ng/mL was reported in one index case. This dosage branch must not be generalized to sequence variants with normal or reduced secretion.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-Gene Duplication of PCSK9 as a Novel Genetic Mechanism for Severe Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Features in affected individuals included severely elevated LDL cholesterol levels that were refractory to intensive statin therapy, pronounced clinical stigmata, premature cardiovascular events, and a plasma PCSK9 of approximately 5000 ng/mL in 1 index case.

nodes.description: PCSK9 promotes receptor delivery to lysosomes and loss of LDLR protein. PCSK9 is not asserted to proteolytically cleave LDLR itself. The cited route depends on cell context; uptake into mouse embryonic fibroblasts did not produce the same receptor loss.

evidence.reference_title: Effect of mutations in the PCSK9 gene on the cell surface LDL receptors.
evidence.snippet: The two gain-of-function mutations had a 23% decreased level of cell surface LDLR and a 38% decreased level of internalization of LDL as compared with WT-PCSK9.

evidence.snippet: PCSK9 mutation dramatically increased the production rate of apolipoprotein B100 (3-fold) compared with controls or LDL-R mutated subjects, related to direct overproduction of VLDL (3-fold), IDL (3-fold), and LDL (5-fold).

evidence.snippet: This suggests that the variants of PCSK9 found in FH influence the secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins, providing an explanation for the marked increase in circulating LDL in heterozygous carriers.

nodes.description: One of the two founding ADH3 alleles. Markedly impairs autocatalytic zymogen processing and reduces cell-surface LDL receptor in patient lymphoblasts.

evidence.reference_title: NARC-1/PCSK9 and its natural mutants: zymogen cleavage and effects on the low density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor and LDL cholesterol.
evidence.snippet: The cell surface LDL receptor (LDLR) levels are reduced by 35% in lymphoblasts of S127R patients.

nodes.description: Rare copy-number mechanism reported in two unrelated index cases with cosegregation in affected relatives. Very high plasma PCSK9 was measured in one index case; treatment resistance is not a universal prediction.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-Gene Duplication of PCSK9 as a Novel Genetic Mechanism for Severe Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: We identified a whole-gene duplication of PCSK9 in 2 unrelated Canadian FH index cases; this PCSK9 CNV was also found to cosegregate with affected status in family members.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-Gene Duplication of PCSK9 as a Novel Genetic Mechanism for Severe Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Features in affected individuals included severely elevated LDL cholesterol levels that were refractory to intensive statin therapy, pronounced clinical stigmata, premature cardiovascular events, and a plasma PCSK9 of approximately 5000 ng/mL in 1 index case.

nodes.description: Pathogenic heterozygous sequence variants and rare whole-gene duplication cause PCSK9-related FH. Their biochemical effects differ; altered processing alone does not distinguish gain from loss of function. Candidate reporter variants are not equated with clinically established alleles.
nodes.id: Pathogenic PCSK9 Sequence Variant or Duplication

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PCSK9 cause autosomal dominant hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: We mapped a third locus associated with ADH, HCHOLA3 at 1p32, and now report two mutations in the gene PCSK9 (encoding proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) that cause ADH.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-Gene Duplication of PCSK9 as a Novel Genetic Mechanism for Severe Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: We identified a whole-gene duplication of PCSK9 in 2 unrelated Canadian FH index cases; this PCSK9 CNV was also found to cosegregate with affected status in family members.

genetic_context.description: Established heterozygous PCSK9 gain-of-function sequence variants or dosage increase from whole-gene duplication. Variant-specific biochemical activity must be distinguished from increased abundance of otherwise wild-type protein.

nodes.description: Peripheral arterial stenosis can occur. It was recorded in 2 of 96 assessed carriers in a selected multicentre PCSK9 cohort. Broader FH studies also show increased peripheral arterial disease; these observations do not establish a population frequency for ADH3.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia and Risk of Peripheral Arterial Disease and Chronic Kidney Disease.
evidence.snippet: Compared with individuals with unlikely FH, multivariable adjusted ORs (95% CIs) of PAD were 1.84 (1.70 to 2.00) in those with possible FH and 1.36 (1.00 to 1.84) in individuals with probable/definite FH.

evidence.reference_title: Coronary Heart Disease, Peripheral Arterial Disease, and Stroke in Familial Hypercholesterolaemia: Insights From the SAFEHEART Registry (Spanish Familial Hypercholesterolaemia Cohort Study).
evidence.snippet: Coronary artery-related manifestations and peripheral artery disease were more prevalent in FH patients than in controls, but no significant differences were found for cerebrovascular events.

nodes.description: Premature coronary atherosclerosis is an important complication. The more-than-ten-year difference from selected LDLR carriers was observed in the small British D374Y cohort and is not a universal age-of-onset difference for PCSK9 variants.

evidence.reference_title: Severe hypercholesterolemia in four British families with the D374Y mutation in the PCSK9 gene: long-term follow-up and treatment response.
evidence.snippet: and were affected >10 years earlier by premature coronary artery disease (35.2+/-4.8 versus 46.8+/-8.9 years; P=0.002)

evidence.reference_title: Binding of proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 to epidermal growth factor-like repeat A of low density lipoprotein receptor decreases receptor recycling and increases degradation.
evidence.snippet: Gain-of-function mutations in PCSK9 cause hypercholesterolemia and premature atherosclerosis, whereas loss-of-function mutations result in hypocholesterolemia and protection from heart disease.

nodes.description: Hepatic expression supplies variant PCSK9 or additional wild-type protein after gene duplication. This is the synthesis step targeted by RNA silencing. It does not assert increased synthesis or secretion for every allele: S127R hepatocyte-like cells secreted less protein despite impaired LDL uptake. Intracellular and extracellular actions need not share a secretion requirement.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PCSK9 cause autosomal dominant hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: PCSK9 encodes NARC-1 (neural apoptosis regulated convertase), a newly identified human subtilase that is highly expressed in the liver and contributes to cholesterol homeostasis.

evidence.reference_title: Urine-sample-derived human induced pluripotent stem cells as a model to study PCSK9-mediated autosomal dominant hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: cells originally derived from an individual with ADH (HLC-S127R) secreted less PCSK9 in the media (-38.5%; P=0.038) and had a 71% decrease (P<0.001) of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) uptake

nodes.description: Reduced receptor availability impairs hepatocyte LDL uptake. Patient-derived cell uptake and human isotope-derived LDL catabolic rates support related but distinct aspects of this route; neither assay alone measures all liver flux.
nodes.id: Reduced Hepatic Clearance of Circulating LDL Particles

animal_models.description: Transgenic pigs show the receptor-depletion-to-clearance-failure step directly, with both hepatic LDL receptor level and LDL clearance measured in the same animals.
animal_models.genotype: Liver-specific expression of human PCSK9 p.Asp374Tyr (Sleeping Beauty transposition, somatic cell nuclear transfer)
animal_models.name: D374Y-PCSK9 transgenic Yucatan minipig

evidence.reference_title: Urine-sample-derived human induced pluripotent stem cells as a model to study PCSK9-mediated autosomal dominant hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: cells originally derived from an individual with ADH (HLC-S127R) secreted less PCSK9 in the media (-38.5%; P=0.038) and had a 71% decrease (P<0.001) of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) uptake

evidence.reference_title: Apolipoprotein B100 metabolism in autosomal-dominant hypercholesterolemia related to mutations in PCSK9.
evidence.snippet: LDL fractional catabolic rate was slightly decreased (by 30%) compared with controls but still higher than LDL-R-mutated subjects.

experimental_models.description: Hepatocyte-like cells carrying the patient's S127R allele take up 71% less LDL than control cells, the cellular readout of this node.
experimental_models.name: Urine-derived iPSC hepatocyte-like cells from a PCSK9 S127R carrier (HLC-S127R)

nodes.description: Enhanced receptor loss decreases the surface LDLR pool. Surface abundance is a separate readout from lysosomal location, LDLR transcription and whole-body LDL clearance.
nodes.id: Reduced Hepatocyte Surface LDL Receptor Abundance

evidence.reference_title: Effect of mutations in the PCSK9 gene on the cell surface LDL receptors.
evidence.snippet: The two gain-of-function mutations had a 23% decreased level of cell surface LDLR and a 38% decreased level of internalization of LDL as compared with WT-PCSK9.

nodes.description: PCSK9 association reduces the return of internalized LDL receptor to the cell surface. Interference with an acid-dependent receptor conformational change is a proposed explanation rather than a directly resolved molecular intermediate in the cited study.

evidence.reference_title: Binding of proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 to epidermal growth factor-like repeat A of low density lipoprotein receptor decreases receptor recycling and increases degradation.
evidence.snippet: These data are consistent with a model in which PCSK9 binding to EGF-A interferes with an acid-dependent conformational change required for receptor recycling.

nodes.description: Selected prodomain and C-terminal variants impair PCSK9 association with LDL particles in vitro. LDL can inhibit extracellular receptor-depleting activity in the tested systems. How much this regulatory association contributes to each human phenotype remains unresolved; reduced particle binding is not increased binding to LDLR.
nodes.id: Reduced PCSK9 Association with LDL Particles

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic gain-of-function mutations in the prodomain and C-terminal domain of PCSK9 inhibit LDL binding.
evidence.snippet: Herein, we identify additional GOF mutations that inhibit LDL association, localized either within CM1 or a surface-exposed region in the PCSK9 prodomain.

nodes.description: Physical inactivity is a modifiable FH risk factor. An observational composite of diet, exercise, smoking and weight cannot estimate the effect of changing exercise alone.

evidence.reference_title: Association of the Interaction Between Familial Hypercholesterolemia Variants and Adherence to a Healthy Lifestyle With Risk of Coronary Artery Disease.
evidence.snippet: Among carriers, a favorable lifestyle conferred 86% lower risk of CAD compared with an unfavorable lifestyle (hazard ratio, 0.14 [95% CI, 0.04-0.41]).

nodes.description: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition is foundational FH therapy. Response varies: selected D374Y carriers remained severely hypercholesterolemic despite treatment, while a small S127R series had substantial LDL-C lowering. These observations do not establish universal PCSK9-related statin resistance.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Adults: pharmacotherapy (statins with additional medications as needed) to reduce lipid levels; referral to a lipid specialist if necessary to reduce LDL-C levels

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Children: referral to a lipid specialist; diet and lifestyle modifications; statins can be used in children starting around age eight years.

evidence.reference_title: FDA requests removal of strongest warning against using cholesterol-lowering statins during pregnancy; still advises most pregnant patients should stop taking statins | FDA
evidence.snippet: Health care professionals should discontinue statin therapy in most pregnant patients. Alternatively, health care professionals should consider the ongoing therapeutic needs of the individual patient

evidence.reference_title: Update on familial hypercholesterolemia: An expert clinical consensus from the National Lipid Association.
evidence.snippet: A stepwise approach to optimal therapy is outlined, beginning with lifestyle interventions and pharmacotherapy with maximally tolerated statins and ezetimibe.

nodes.description: ApoB particles entering susceptible arterial regions can be retained in the intima. Endothelial state, particle modification and inflammation influence subsequent lesion development; retention alone does not imply an immediate symptomatic stenosis.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis - Endotext - NCBI Bookshelf
evidence.snippet: Indeed, infiltration and retention of apoB containing lipoproteins in the artery wall is a critical initiating event that sparks an inflammatory response and promotes the development of atherosclerosis.

nodes.description: Cholesterol deposits in tendons, classically the Achilles tendon and the extensor tendons of the hands, worsening with age.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Xanthomas (cholesterol deposits in tendons) may be visible in the Achilles tendons or tendons of the hands and worsen with age as a result of extremely high cholesterol levels.

nodes.description: Smoking is a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor in FH. Its contribution is not assumed to be independent of every lipid measure.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia-Risk-Score: A New Score Predicting Cardiovascular Events and Cardiovascular Mortality in Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: The FH-Risk-Score incorporates 7 clinical variables: sex, age, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, hypertension, smoking, and lipoprotein (a) (Lp(a)) with a Harrell C-index for 10-year ASCVD event of 0.75

nodes.description: Urine-derived cells from one S127R carrier were reprogrammed into iPSCs and differentiated into hepatocyte-like cells. One healthy donor supplied the comparator; multiple clones are not independent patients. The nonisogenic comparison supports a patient-cell phenotype without isolating the variant from donor background.
nodes.id: Urine-derived iPSC hepatocyte-like cells from a PCSK9 S127R carrier (HLC-S127R)

evidence.reference_title: Urine-sample-derived human induced pluripotent stem cells as a model to study PCSK9-mediated autosomal dominant hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: urine samples provide an attractive and convenient source of somatic cells for reprogramming and hepatocyte differentiation, but also a powerful tool to further decipher PCSK9 mutations and function.

nodes.description: Plaque-associated mediators can stimulate smooth-muscle-cell proliferation. This is a conserved atherosclerosis process inferred downstream of lipid accumulation, not a directly measured response to every PCSK9 allele.

biological_processes: positive regulation of smooth muscle cell proliferation

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis - Endotext - NCBI Bookshelf
evidence.snippet: Macrophage inflammatory chemoattractants stimulate infiltration and proliferation of smooth muscle cells.

nodes.description: Yellowish waxy cholesterol deposits around the eyelids.

evidence.reference_title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
evidence.snippet: Xanthelasmas (yellowish, waxy deposits) can occur around the eyelids.
